title: Normalize incomplete billing sink events to restore per-model consumption charts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Over the past three weeks we've observed per-model consumption charts in the Console under-reporting usage and showing a growing 'unattributed' / 'unknown model' bucket. Root cause appears to be incomplete billing sink events that arrive without a canonical model_id when downstream rate limiting or partial ingestion occurs. The missing model_id causes the analytics pipeline to attribute tokens to an 'unattributed' bucket, which skews per-model trends, quota reporting, and automated billing rollups.

Observed behavior: console shows spikes in 'unattributed' tokens, per-model totals are lower than billing invoices for several enterprise customers, delayed ingestion events (late-arriving) sometimes contain only request_id and token counts but lack model metadata, and a recent SDK change to retry semantics correlated with an increase in partial sink writes. This ticket is to define, implement, and validate an event-normalization + backfill approach and small Console UX change to prevent noisy dashboards while we repair historical data.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model totals in Console align with billing sink aggregate totals to within 0.5% for the last 30 days after backfill
New streaming events with missing model_id are normalized at ingest so that the unattributed bucket no longer grows beyond expected noise levels
Console shows a temporary 'Pending attribution' state for late events so customers are not misled by transient unattributed spikes
Backfill job is idempotent, resumable, and completes within SLA (48 hours for 90% of tenant data)
Monitoring and alerting for normalization failures are in place (Pager duty if >10% of events fail normalization for 1 hour)
proposed_solution: Build an Event Normalizer microservice in the billing ingestion tier that: 1) looks up model_id by request_id using the recent-request index; 2) canonicalizes model names (model_id/version) and owner tags; 3) emits a normalized event to the analytics stream even when original sink lacks model metadata.
Add a small conservative mapping table (recent_request_map) with TTL 7 days keyed by request_id -> model_id populated by the API front-end and runtime emitters to support late-attribution lookups.

Implement an idempotent daily backfill job that reprocesses the last 90 days of raw sink records with missing model_id and re-inserts normalized events into the timeseries store; job to run in batches with rate limits to avoid DB overload.

Console UX change: introduce a 'Pending attribution' placeholder series for charts and a hover note that explains late/backfilled events; by default this series is collapsed for non-admins to reduce noise.

Update quota and billing rollup logic to ignore unattributed counts for enforcement decisions until normalization completes to avoid false quota breaches; after backfill, reconcile enforcement windows.
Add alerting on the normalization pipeline and a dashboard showing the percentage of unattributed events over time and per-tenant breakdown so we can triage regressions quickly.
work_log: 2026-03-01 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after customer ops flagged multiple customers with mismatched per-model dashboard totals vs invoice. Linked billing ledger query and sample unattributed events (see links).

2026-03-03 David Chen: Reproduced locally with sample sink dump. Confirmed presence of records missing 'model_id' and that request_id exists in the request_log table for many of these. Opened spike to test request_id lookup latency.

2026-03-05 David Chen: Spike demo: request_id -> model_id lookup is sub-5ms for hot keys but can miss if request_log GC TTL < sink delay; recommending increasing recent_request_map TTL and populating earlier in request lifecycle.
2026-03-07 Design review (Marta Ruiz): Suggested UX wording for 'Pending attribution' and default collapsed state for non-admins. Draft copy uploaded to Confluence.
2026-03-09 Engineering sync: Agreed on normalization service design, backfill approach, and monitoring signals. Assigned sub-tasks for normalizer (ENG-20722) and backfill job (ENG-20723).
2026-03-12 David Chen: Implemented prototype event normalizer and integration test harness. End-to-end tests pass on staging with synthetic delayed events. Preparing PR for review.
ui_changes: Add a tertiary series 'Pending attribution' to per-model charts with low-contrast dashed line and explanatory tooltip
Default collapse/hidden state for 'Pending attribution' for Viewer role; Admins and Billing roles see it expanded
Add a banner on the usage page 'We are normalizing late-arriving events — per-model totals may change during the backfill window' with link to status doc
Add fine-grained filter to exclude pending/unattributed events from export or CSV downloads until normalization completes
testing_plan: Unit tests for normalizer: request_id lookup, canonicalization rules, and idempotency checks
Integration tests on staging: inject synthetic delayed sink events (with and without model_id) and assert normalized events appear in timeseries store with correct model_id
Load test backfill job in staging with production-like data shape to validate batching and DB rate limits
End-to-end verification: compare console per-model totals to billing ledger for sample tenants before and after backfill
Run A/B comparison on a subset of tenants: enable normalization for 10% and measure unattributed bucket shrink and per-model alignment
rollback_plan: Feature flag normalizer; default to off. If normalization causes regressions, toggle off which stops normalization of new events (does not delete normalized historic events)
Backfill job writes to new timeseries namespace until validated; if discrepancies found, do not merge namespace and run reconciliation tooling
If console UX causes confusion, revert banner and pending series in a single UI patch release (console-2026.03.rev1)
Coordinate with Billing and Support teams before any public-facing changes; communicate rollback to affected customers.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: recent_request_map may grow large and become a hotspot. Mitigation: set per-tenant rate limits, sharded cache, and evict non-hot keys aggressively.
Risk: backfill may overload timeseries DB. Mitigation: batch windowed backfill, monitor DB CPU/IO, and implement graceful slowdown.

Risk: normalization errors could misattribute events. Mitigation: conservative canonicalization rules, require 2 independent signals (request_id and timestamp proximity) for assignment when ambiguous.
Risk: quota enforcement divergence during migration. Mitigation: freeze enforcement on unattributed counts during backfill window and reconcile after backfill completes.
communication_plan: Notify internal Billing and Support channels with weekly progress updates and an escalation path
Prepare customer-facing status note for affected tenants with expected timeline and impact reduction steps
Create a short post-mortem after backfill completes documenting root cause, actions taken, and persistent prevention measures
